evidence.quoted_text:
def test_post_boundary_activation_refusal_is_required(self):
        phases = self._phases()
        manager = {"before": self._snapshot(10, "i1", "boot-1"),
                   "after": self._snapshot(11, "i2", "boot-1"),
                   "after_phase": {"direct": {"rc": 0},
                                   "dependency": {"rc": 1}}}
        reboot = {"before": self._snapshot(11, "i2", "boot-1"),
                  "after": self._snapshot(12, "i3", "boot-2"),
                  "after_phase": {"direct": {"rc": 1},
                                  "dependency": {"rc": 0}},
                  "boot_id_before": "boot-1", "boot_id_after": "boot-2",
                  "qemu_pid_before": 99, "qemu_pid_after": 99,
                  "qemu_identity_verified": True}
        checks = vm.build_checks(phases, manager, reboot)
        self.assertFalse(checks["mask_persisted"])
evidence.reason: The current test still combines both post-boundary refusal conditions in one fixture and asserts only `checks["mask_persisted"]` is false. Because the manager-restart direct activation returns 0 and the reboot dependency activation returns 0, `build_checks` could ignore either boundary and the test would still pass. The two refusals need independent cases with both boundaries initially valid and one return code changed at a time.
